title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore West on 1970-06-04
source: Audience Recording by Gerry Olsen. Sony TC-124 single-capstan portable cassette deck equipped with Sony F-99S One Point Stereo Dynamic Microphone IMP LOW (hand-held). 120 minute BASF normal bias tape. Lineage via Dan McDonald (droncit@yahoo.com): Master Audience Cassette->Nakamichi BX-1 (modified for flat transfer)-> Tascam DR-07MK2 (24-bit, 96kHz); DC8Forensics was used to apply the NAB curve for normal bias cassettes. Converted to 16-bit, 44.1kHz using 32-bit interpolation and a triangular high pass dither. After the NAB curve in a multifilter I applied a virtual vale and overtone generator for lost harmonics and used a channel blender to blend below 150 Hz to mono to minimize mic handling noise.

ai_review.summary: Clear, superior audience recording of a three‑part June 4 1970 Fillmore West show with standout St. Stephen → Not Fade Away → Midnight Hour sequence
ai_review.review: The tape captures an exceptional mid‑70s performance – acoustic set, New Riders of the Purple Sage, and a blistering electric second half – highlighted by the smoking St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour medley and tight China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider transition.  Though it’s primarily an audience recording (with some soundboard bits), reviewers praise its surprising clarity and recommend modest EQ tweaks.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is ~4.3 stars; comments overwhelmingly praise both the show (standout jams, seamless set flow) and the recording’s clarity, with only one mixed‑feel review.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Very clear upfront sound for an audience tape; some matrixed bits (soundboard portions of first set) and occasional EQ adjustments recommended. No major drop‑outs reported.

standout_songs: St. Stephen > Not Fade Away > Midnight Hour
China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑part flow (acoustic → NRPS → electric) is praised for its seamless transitions; the acoustic and NRPS sets build nicely into a high‑energy electric half, though one reviewer finds NRPS a novelty.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his pedal steel work with NRRS and versatile guitar/steel performance across all three sets.
band_member_comments.Drums: Mickey's drumming described as ‘decidedly non‑country country’ and adds energy to the NRPS set; overall drum work receives positive nods.
